correctness.rationale: For n≥4 full standard Euclidean D_n Coxeter fan, rays are Weyl images of fundamental weights. Distinct two-ray cones correspond bijectively to ridges; counting via standard parabolic stabilizers gives the ordinary–ordinary, ordinary–spin, and spin–spin multiplicities. Fundamental-weight Euclidean products give normal cosines √(k/ℓ), √(k/n), and (n−2)/n respectively. Each interior angle is π−acos(cosine). Summing orbits gives R_n=5^n−2·3^n+1−n4^{n−1}+n2^{n−1}. Binomial k↔ℓ−k symmetry cancels central ordinary contributions; omitted fork/spin terms combine into total centered angle −πn2^{n−3}, giving exact mean 3π/4−πn2^{n−3}/R_n, asymptotic positive deficit (πn/8)(2/5)^n. Independent exact rational Gram calculations verified n=4,5,6 multiplicity tables and counts 240,1440,8216, with further numerical mean checks. Nonstandard all-n combinatorial conclusion follows from Coxeter stabilizers and binomial identities rather than the checker.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A theorem covering all type-B fans is not a stronger theorem for type-D fans. General Coxeter face counts do not by themselves specify Euclidean angles without additional Gram calculations.
